claims.claim: The 3-minute load is a storage-format problem, not a language problem, and C++ would not fix it.
claims.about: Python vs C++ for loading a 4 GB index
claims.why: The start-up figures are for empty servers (python-flask 996 ms, cpp-drogon 295 ms), not for parsing or loading a multi-GB data structure.

claims.claim: Startup becomes effectively instant (opening a read-only file instead of loading the index into Python objects)
claims.why: A Flask server that loads no data starts in about 0.6–1 s, which is effectively instant next to the current 3 minutes.

claims.claim: Full C++ service: the lookup would be fast
claims.why: The lookup speed of a custom in-memory index isn't measured; only the HTTP framework overhead is.

claims.claim: Python's per-request overhead is small compared with the 50 ms budget, so C++ doesn't buy you much here.
claims.measured: python-flask plaintext 1,732 req/s per core (~0.6 ms CPU per request), gthread 4,031 req/s (~0.25 ms); cpp-drogon 85,540 req/s
claims.why: Flask spends about 0.25–0.6 ms of CPU per request, far below 50 ms, so Drogon being about 20–50x faster per request matters little at 100 req/s.

claims.claim: Flask under gunicorn with about 4 workers can serve the 100 lookups/second target, which is easy if most lookups are small
claims.measured: python-flask 1,732 req/s plaintext and 1,529 req/s for a single-row DB lookup on 1 CPU; gthread 4,031 / 2,119 req/s
claims.why: Even the slowest Flask setup measured more than 10x the 100 req/s target on a single core.

claims.claim: Python object overhead can make a 4 GB file take well over 10 GB in RAM; four workers each holding a copy would exhaust a 16 GB VM
claims.why: Peak memory was measured only for trivial handlers (about 41–123 MB for Python), not for large in-memory data structures.

claims.claim: A NumPy memory-mapped array with binary search gets close to C speed without any server-side C++
claims.why: No benchmark covers NumPy or memory-mapped array lookups.

claims.claim: Serverless functions: each cold start would reload the index
claims.why: Serverless platforms and their cold starts weren't measured.
